# pingtable

> Pingtable is a free host monitor with a live table, command line, local
> HTTP API and MCP server. It monitors ICMP replies and named TCP services
> such as example.com:443, measures latency and traces routes. Its source
> is available under Apache 2.0.

Checks are sent from the computer pingtable runs on. Use it only on hosts the
user owns or is allowed to test.

## For agents

- [Using pingtable from an AI agent](https://github.com/lorincz-llc/pingtable/blob/main/docs/ai-agents.md): the MCP server (`pingtable-cli mcp`), its tools with arguments and example results, which tool to use when, limits.
- [The local HTTP API](https://github.com/lorincz-llc/pingtable/blob/main/docs/api.md): every call with request and reply examples; `pingtable-cli api` prints the address and token.

## Quick reference

- MCP server command: `pingtable-cli mcp` (standard input and output; tools only). Add `--allow-add` to offer `table_add_hosts`.
- Tools: `ping`, `trace_route`, `network_info`, `table_status`; `table_add_hosts` only with `--allow-add`.
- `ping` takes plain names and addresses and at most one range or block (256 hosts). Every call ends within 30 seconds.
- For JSON from the command line, run `pingtable-cli once --format json HOST...`. Use `example.com:443` to check a named TCP service once. Exit status is 0 when every host answers, 1 for a failed check and 2 for invalid input.

## More

- [README](https://github.com/lorincz-llc/pingtable/blob/main/README.md): what the app does, host list syntax, how it works.
